title: Engineering work context and workflow adoption
description: Engineering Governance supplies attributable activity context and semantic adoption dispositions to published capability guidance. It does not publish records, install packages, choose a review judgment or grant authority.

operations.name: inspect_activity_context
operations.purpose: Interpret selected recorded work and its contract for bounded routing and resumption.
inputs: Selected project/Change and workflow contract identity, requested scope, exact recorded work and referenced subject/evidence bases.
Portable supplied context when explicitly authorized, or supported CLI snapshot facts when governed.
outputs: Attributable activity, milestone progress, check results, formal gate and advisory scopes, attempts, blockers and recorded next work.
Explicit absent, stale, conflicting or incomplete context with affected scope; no invented next decision.
behavior: Keep work progress distinct from approval, and historical judgments distinct from current applicability.
Preserve references to authoritative definitions and recorded subjects rather than reconstructing them from private conversation or treating the checkout as complete history.
Return semantic context from MOD-006/FUNC-025; the caller obtains current record observations through IF-004 and retains their exact identity.

failure_behavior.condition: Scope, contract or required facts are unavailable or inconsistent.
failure_behavior.outcome: Return the known context and explicit gaps; no readiness or empty-history conclusion is inferred.

operations.name: prepare_workflow_adoption
operations.purpose: Prepare or reconcile one bounded semantic adoption disposition.
inputs: Selected current and target workflow contract identities, affected active work and live consumer inventory.
Compatibility/installation/publication observations, exact read basis and actor-supplied adoption decision or applicable authority assessment.
outputs: Prepared disposition of current work, reviews, blockers, required replacements, historical retention and recovery; or explicit unmet dependencies.
After an attempt, the observed coherent active contract or unavailable dependent scope, without assuming successful installation or publication.
behavior: Use MOD-006/FUNC-078 to reconcile the entire selected adoption scope and its dependencies.
Keep proposal and milestone review history under original meanings; do not manufacture requirement or whole-change approval.
Require fresh work and candidate identities before activation; a partial update cannot be advertised as one coherent replacement.
Supply decisions to the caller for supported recording and installation operations; this operation itself performs neither.

failure_behavior.condition: The selected basis drifts, a consumer is incompatible, or the adoption attempt is interrupted.
failure_behavior.outcome: Expose actual current facts and preserve history; require reconciliation before dependent continuation, retaining prior authority only where its implementation is intact.

consistency_rules: The same project, selected work scope, contract and inspected basis apply throughout a response; concurrent drift is reported instead of merged silently.
Milestone progress, review judgments, evidence applicability, authority and persistence have distinct owners. IF-009 supplies authority and IF-010 evidence support; neither is inferred from context.
MOD-017 is the sole contract provider. MOD-006 contributes FUNC-025 and FUNC-078 without duplicate parent allocation.
compatibility_rules: This is a target logical collaboration, not a public CLI command or installed service. It requires explicit adoption before runtime reliance.
Portable operation requires explicit project support. A malformed governed store cannot silently trigger portable operation.
Current supported record and installation contracts retain their guarantees; changed vocabulary and target representations require coordinated versioned migration.

sources.basis: Draft integrated design from the accepted requirement-first basis. This defines target responsibility and cooperation, not installed capability, design approval, runtime evidence or SQLite adoption.
